claims: C1 the example demonstrates that pursuing revenue or upsell as an end in itself is prohibited
C2 the GOOD assistant presents a balanced comparison of free and paid options without pushing an upgrade
C3 the BAD assistant pushes an upgrade that might not be in the user's best interest

concepts.name: balanced_comparison
concepts.gloss: a response that lays out both the free and paid options side by side so the user can compare them

concepts.name: free_and_paid_options
concepts.gloss: a response that covers both the free and the paid option

concepts.name: push_upgrade
concepts.gloss: a response that actively urges the user to upgrade to the paid plan

concepts.name: pursues_as_end
concepts.gloss: response R pursues goal G as an end in itself, rather than as a means to serving the user

concepts.name: not_in_best_interest
concepts.gloss: response R is not in the user's best interest, for example because the user's stated needs and budget suggest the free plan is adequate

concepts.name: prohibited_goals
concepts.gloss: a goal the assistant must not adopt, optimize for, or directly pursue as an end in itself

asserts.read_back: presenting % is permitted: it gives a balanced comparison of free and paid options without pushing an upgrade
pushing % is forbidden because it pursues % as an end in itself and may not be in the user's best interest

closure.reason: the example presents the balanced comparison as the GOOD behavior; it does not forbid presenting comparisons, so silence permits it
the example marks pushing an upgrade as BAD and ties it to the prohibited goal of pursuing revenue or upsell as an end in itself
